StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

InstanceType.issue: PowerInstanceType.Instanced (WitheringPresencePower.cs:26): C# creates one instance per OPPONENT, each with its own `Target` (Aeonglass.cs:78-83 loops `GetOpponentsOf(base.Creature)`), and the counter is per-instance. The sim's stacking check always behaves as PowerInstanceType.None. power_cmd gap G5 owns the mechanism and this is one of its 11 named ported instances -- and one of the seven that do not acknowledge the distinction at all. DORMANT by scope: one player means one opponent means one instance, so like power/strangle this is dormant BY SCOPE rather than by content and will not become live by porting more Ironclad content. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: The mechanism is right -- count the target player's card plays down from 6, add a Wither to HAND at 0, reset to 6 -- and the Wither's upgrade matching is preserved (`aeonglass.MatchWitherToUpgradeCount(wither)` at WitheringPresencePower.cs:37 vs powers.py:3287-3288's `for _ in range(wither_upgrade_count): wither.fake_upgrade()`). Two findings. (1) The COUNTER'S IDENTITY is conflated: C# keeps `CardsLeft` as a DynamicVar whose canonical default is 6 (WitheringPresencePower.cs:16,28) and resets it to the LITERAL `6m` (:57), entirely independent of `base.Amount`; the sim initialises and resets `_cards_left` from `self.amount` (powers.py:3274, 3283). Those coincide only because both appliers pass 6 -- Aeonglass.cs:82 applies `6m` and monsters/glory/aeonglass.py:19,40 applies `_WITHERING_PRESENCE = 6` -- so a Withering Presence applied at any other amount, or STACKED (StackType is Counter, so stacking really does raise Amount), would reset to the wrong number in the sim and to 6 in the game. DORMANT, by enumeration of the two appliers. (2) hook_dispatch gap G4: the sim fires on_card_played once per play where C# fires AfterCardPlayed once per CardPlay iteration, so a Throwing-Axe- or One-Two-Punch-doubled card advances the counter by 1 in the sim and by 2 in the game -- G4 is already LIVE with an executed witness and is not re-verdicted; the per-unit consequence is that Wither arrives later in the sim. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: The sim has no per-instance Target and tests nothing (powers.py:3276-3277), which is equivalent in single-player -- every played card belongs to the one player. Folded into the InstanceType finding.
